phases.message: It's holiday hiring and I'm behind on WOTC. Start here in Talentry: go through every hire since November, their screening answers, their age, and when they signed the 8850 against when we offered the job.
Now Payroll Harbor. Note the day each of them actually began work, and anything about their history with us.
My Mailnest hiring folder has what people sent us: benefit letters, the VA, release papers, and a few notes. Read what bears on the credit.
This is WorkCredit Online. Submit an 8850 for every hire who qualifies and is still inside the 28 days, with the right group, then tell me who you left out and why.

rules.text: Today is Friday 12 December 2025. WorkCredit Online takes Form 8850 with ETA Form 9061 for the Work Opportunity Tax Credit (IRC §51). Topics: deadline, groups, exclusions, hours. One submission per hire. The credit is for people who begin work on or before 31 December 2025, the end date in the law as it stands.

Submit no later than the 28th day after the day the person began work: a start on 17 November is due by 15 December. A late submission cannot be certified, and the credit for that hire is lost. The applicant must sign Form 8850 on or before the day the job was offered; a form signed after the offer cannot be certified. Someone who never began work has no start date and no credit.

Code: who (maximum credit). SNAP: aged 18 to 39, household received SNAP for the 6 months before hire, or 3 of the last 5 ($2,400). VET-UNEMP4: veteran unemployed 4 weeks to under 6 months in the year before hire ($2,400). VET-UNEMP6: veteran unemployed 6 months or more in that year ($5,600). VET-DIS: veteran with a service-connected disability, hired within a year of discharge ($4,800). VET-DIS-UNEMP6: veteran with a service-connected disability, unemployed 6 months or more in the year before hire ($9,600). LTUR: unemployed 27 consecutive weeks or more, with unemployment compensation for some of it ($2,400). EXFELON: hired within a year of a felony conviction or of release from prison ($2,400). SSI: received SSI for any month ending in the 60 days before hire ($2,400). VR: referred by vocational rehabilitation ($2,400). A hire who fits several groups is submitted under the one worth most.

No credit, so do not submit: a relative of the employer or of an owner of more than 50% (child, grandchild, brother or sister, parent, nephew or niece, aunt or uncle, in-laws: IRC §51(i)(1) and §152(d)(2)); anyone the employer employed at any time before (§51(i)(2)), so no rehires; anyone in no group.

The credit is 40% of first-year wages up to the group's cap once the person has worked 400 hours, 25% from 120 to 399 hours, and nothing under 120. A hire scheduled 30 hours a week or more passes 400 hours in about three months. Enter the group's maximum credit on the form; the employer claims the actual credit on Form 5884 after the year.
